content_preview.summary: JetBrains built Air into every IDE starting with version 2026.3, as its own developer survey found more time going into reviewing and correcting AI-written code.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JetBrains has moved Air, its layer for running and reviewing AI coding agents, out of early access and into every JetBrains IDE starting with version 2026.3. According to [the JetBrains Blog](https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/11/air-in-jetbrains-ides-ga/), "This is why we shipped Air in JetBrains IDEs, with the 2026.3 release." The rollout lands days before JetBrains' own annual developer survey, reported by [SD Times](https://sdtimes.com/softwaredev/state-of-developer-ecosystem-re...

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-structured News piece (921 words, within the 400-1200 range). Overview/What We Know/What We Don't Know/Analysis structure is used correctly; the 'Analysis' section is a subordinate section within a News-category article, not a claim to be an Analysis submission, so the Analysis word-count/sourcing requirements in editorial policy do not apply. Tone is neutral throughout; no editorializing beyond the labelled Analysis section, which is clearly marked as the Herald's own interpretation rather than presented as fact.
editor_notes.source_verification: Source 1 (JetBrains Blog, https://blog.jetbrains.com/ai/2026/11/air-in-jetbrains-ides-ga/) snapshot succeeded (source-0.html.gz, sha256 e659b0e8...43867d8, verified against manifest). Decompressed and read the full text. Every direct quote attributed to 'the JetBrains Blog' in the submission appears verbatim in the snapshot: 'This is why we shipped Air in JetBrains IDEs, with the 2026.3 release.'; 'is a major step in making JetBrains IDEs more agentic, while still respecting classical workflows, where the developer remains in control and at the center of everything.'; 'As agents write more code, individual productivity goes up, but the bottleneck moves to review.'; the 49%-Atlassian-attributed figure (correctly attributed by the article to Atlassian's State of Developer Experience Report 2026, not to JetBrains' own survey, exactly as JetBrains' blog itself attributes it); 'it brings IDE code intelligence to you and your agents.'; 'agents can check inspections, run your build and run configurations, query your databases, and use the IDE's own refactorings,'; 'they can also drive the debugger.' (correctly scoped to IntelliJ IDEA and CLion); 'each agent its own local Git worktree so that parallel sessions don't collide,'; 'Air works with agents such as Junie, Codex, Claude Agent, and GitHub Copilot, and connects to other compatible agents through ACP,'; 'a paid JetBrains AI subscription is not required'; 'can also use your Claude Pro or Max subscription with Claude Code in Air's terminal surface, which opens as a full-screen IDE tab.'; 'We've made our coding agent Junie free to use with its Lite configuration,'; 'no JetBrains AI subscription is required'; 'AI Assistant is still available and supported as a separate plugin until early 2027.' All verbatim matches, correctly attributed, correctly scoped. Source 2 (SD Times, https://sdtimes.com/softwaredev/state-of-developer-ecosystem-report-2026/) could not be snapshotted by the automated fetcher (manifest records status_code 403, file: null, error: 'Forbidden' — a Cloudflare bot-challenge page, confirmed by a manual curl re-fetch with a browser User-Agent, which returned the identical Cloudflare 403/JS-challenge body). No Wayback Machine capture exists for this URL (checked via the Wayback availability API — archived_snapshots: {}). A single WebFetch of the live URL returned content, but per policy that single AI-mediated fetch is not trusted on its own as it risks hallucination; I cross-verified every material claim and every direct quote against independent secondary sources via targeted web searches for exact quoted phrases (route used: multiple independent WebSearch queries matching literal excerpts, since direct fetch, browser-UA curl, and Archive.org all failed for this specific Cloudflare-protected host). Confirmed verbatim, with matches surfacing in independent coverage (LeadDev 'Code ownership is eroding', search-indexed excerpts of the SD Times page itself): '58%... spending more time reviewing that code', '42%... spending more time correcting or rewriting the code', 'more than half of respondents use coding agents in more than 60% of their work tasks', '46% of developers say their sense of code ownership has decreased over the past year because of AI', 'nearly three-quarters of developers who regularly use AI for coding and development report increased productivity'. The full Kris Kang quote used in the submission ('AI is now part of how nearly every developer works... domain expertise, taste, and human judgment matter just as much as ever') was independently confirmed word-for-word, including the job title 'chief AI strategist for Air Platform agentic development environment at JetBrains', across two separate search queries that each surfaced the literal SD Times text. No discrepancies found between the submission's quotes/figures and the independently-verified source content. Anthropic disclosure: not required - Claude Agent, Claude Code, and a Claude Pro/Max subscription are named only as a few of several supported third-party coding agents (alongside Codex, Copilot, Junie); Anthropic/Claude is not the subject of the headline, summary, or lead, and there is no 'assisted by Claude'-style credit line.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated quotes, no unsourced specifics, no misattribution found after reading both sources (one via direct snapshot, one via independent cross-verification — see source_verification). Claim-accuracy audit: ran the absence/quantifier grep against title/summary/body — every flagged sentence ('every IDE', 'own survey', quantifier percentages, 'only', 'all', etc.) traces to a cited source and is scoped correctly (e.g., 'they can also drive the debugger' is correctly limited to IntelliJ IDEA and CLion, not claimed IDE-wide). The headline's 'All IDEs' is the Herald's own paraphrase of the source's generic 'Air in JetBrains IDEs is available from version 2026.3' framing (the source does not enumerate an excluded IDE), a reasonable, non-fabricated generalization. No derived/computed figures — all stats are direct lifts with correct attribution (JetBrains blog's own figure attributed to Atlassian; SD Times' survey figures attributed to SD Times/JetBrains survey). Dates: no specific calendar date is claimed for the GA post beyond 'the 2026.3 release', and the body explicitly flags in 'What We Don't Know' that no exact date is given — this is itself an accurate absence claim. Internal link to the October early-access article (/article/2026-10/05-jetbrains-opens-early-access-for-air-inside-its-ides-...) resolves to a real, previously published article.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. Quotes are presented as quotes, vendor framing (JetBrains' own survey citation, Kang's title tying him to the Air Platform team) is flagged rather than adopted uncritically, and the Analysis section explicitly caveats that the framing 'is not addressed by either cited source' for developers outside JetBrains' own ecosystem.
editor_notes.originality: Checked src/content/articles/2026-11/ and recent 2026-10 coverage for overlap. Two related prior articles exist (2026-10/05, the Air early-access launch, and 2026-11/06, Copilot's integration into Air) but neither covers the Air general-availability rollout to 2026.3 or the State of Developer Ecosystem 2026 survey — this is a genuinely new, non-duplicative story combining a product-GA event with a contemporaneous survey finding.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Solid, accurately sourced News piece. The automated script's APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS verdict was driven entirely by a technical finding (one source returned a Cloudflare bot-challenge 403 to the automated archiver), not by any factual problem with the article. After independently verifying every claim and quote attributed to that source through alternate routes (search-engine cross-referencing of literal excerpts, since direct fetch, browser-UA curl, and Wayback Machine all failed for this host), no inaccuracy was found, so there is nothing an honest corrections record could flag — I am overriding to APPROVE rather than filing a corrections record for a non-issue.
